system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: GCP
G2: Azure
G3: Istio/Linkerd in production
G4: CKAD (expired)
G5: line management

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Listing Istio or service mesh because SRE ads ask for it
T2: Listing CKAD
T3: Claiming GCP/Azure for multi-cloud ads
T4: Claiming people management / Engineering Manager
T5: Over-crediting Backstage plugin development
T6: Old cover letter is to her current employer and says she is at Brightwater

# OUTPUT 1: CV
NADIA BRENNAN-AZIZ
Senior Cloud Infrastructure / Platform Engineer
Manchester, UK | nadia.brennanaziz@example.com | +44 7700 900909 | github.com/nba-sre-example
PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Cloud infrastructure and platform engineer with 10 years in infrastructure, including the last 6
running Kubernetes platforms on AWS. Hands-on experience designing, building and operating
production cloud infrastructure, maintaining Terraform-based infrastructure as code, and leading
platform engineering work. Focused on reliable, observable platforms and self-service infrastructure
that helps product teams ship and operate services effectively.
PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
Senior Platform Engineer | Tallybrook Ltd (B2B accounting SaaS) | Manchester /
remote | Apr 2022 - present
• Technical lead of a 5-person platform team operating an AWS EKS platform with 8 clusters,
approximately 350 services and 3 regions.
• Built an internal developer platform with service templates, Argo CD GitOps and
Crossplane-based self-service for RDS, SQS and S3; reduced the time for a new service to reach
production from approximately 2 weeks to under 1 day.
• Introduced SLOs and error budgets for the 20 most critical services; reduced on-call pages per
week by approximately 60%.
• Moved node provisioning to Karpenter with spot instances, reducing EC2 spend by 38%.
• Participate in the incident commander rotation and wrote the incident and post-mortem process.
Site Reliability Engineer | Brightwater Games | Leeds | Jan 2019 - Mar 2022
• Ran AWS game backend infrastructure using EC2, ECS and then EKS for titles with up to 1.2
million daily active players.
• Managed AWS infrastructure as code with Terraform across approximately 40 modules; used
Atlantis for plan and apply on pull requests.
• Replaced a noisy Nagios setup with a Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager and Loki observability
stack.
• Performed pre-launch load testing with k6 and planned capacity for launch days.
Linux Systems Engineer | Pennine Hosting | Sheffield | Jul 2016 - Dec 2018
• Managed approximately 600 Linux servers for hosting customers using Puppet configuration
management.
• Automated tasks with Bash and Python and provided on-call support for customer incidents.
TECHNICAL SKILLS
Cloud and infrastructure: AWS (EKS, EC2, VPC, IAM, RDS, S3, SQS, Route 53, CloudFront),
Terraform, Atlantis, Kubernetes, Helm, Kustomize, Crossplane, Karpenter, Puppet, Linux
Platform and operations: Argo CD, GitHub Actions, Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Alertmanager,
OpenTelemetry, SLOs and error budgets, incident management
Programming and testing: Go, Python, Bash, k6
EDUCATION
BSc Computer Science | University of the North Moors | 2016
CERTIFICATIONS
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) | 2021, renewed 2024
AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Professional | 2023
LANGUAGES
English (native), Urdu (conversational)

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Dear Hiring Manager,
I am applying for the Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor role with Corvale Mobility.
The opportunity to help shape cloud infrastructure for the new train fleet and take it into
production aligns closely with my experience building and operating AWS platforms and
infrastructure-as-code systems.
At Tallybrook, I lead a five-person platform team operating an EKS environment across three
regions. I built a developer platform using service templates, Argo CD GitOps and Crossplane
self-service for AWS services, helping reduce the time to take a new service to production from
around two weeks to under a day. I also introduced SLOs and error budgets for critical services
and contribute to incident command and post-incident processes. This work has centered on
making production services reliable, observable and easier for development teams to run.
Previously, at Brightwater Games, I operated AWS backend infrastructure for titles with up
to 1.2 million daily active players and managed infrastructure as code with Terraform across
approximately 40 modules. I used Atlantis to run plan and apply through pull requests, and
built an observability stack with Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager and Loki. These
experiences offer a strong foundation for Corvale’s cloud infrastructure, system design and
service-operability needs as the vehicle-to-cloud platform develops.
I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my AWS, Terraform, platform engineering
and technical leadership experience could contribute to Corvale’s fleet connectivity work.
Thank you for your consideration.
Yours sincerely, Nadia Brennan-Aziz

Answer for every item id.

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
